title: Grade 4 French — Tue, May 26
description: Verbes en -ER — Day 2 of 5: parler, aimer, habiter in practice
subject: french

questions.question: AIMER means:
questions.explanation: Aimer = to love or to like. J'aime le chocolat = I love chocolate. J'aime jouer = I like playing.

questions.question: HABITER means:
options: To live / to reside (in a place)
questions.explanation: Habiter = to live somewhere. J'habite à Paris = I live in Paris. Takes 'à' before a city.

questions.question: Conjugate AIMER for 'tu':
questions.explanation: AIMER → stem AIM + -es (tu) = tu aimes. 'Tu aimes la musique?' = Do you like music?

questions.question: Conjugate HABITER for 'nous':
questions.explanation: HABITER → stem HABIT + -ons (nous) = nous habitons. 'Nous habitons à Mumbai.'

questions.question: Translate: 'I like dogs.'
questions.explanation: J'aime (I like) + les chiens (dogs, definite plural). 'J'aime les chiens.'

questions.question: Translate: 'We live in London.'
questions.explanation: Nous habitons (we live) + à Londres (in London). 'À' is used before city names with habiter.

questions.question: Fill in: 'Ils ___ le football.' (They like football)
questions.explanation: Ils → -ent ending → ils aiment. 'Ils aiment le football.'

questions.question: Fill in: 'Vous ___ où?' (Where do you live?)
questions.explanation: Vous → -ez ending → vous habitez. 'Vous habitez où?' = Where do you live?

questions.question: Translate: 'She likes to sing.'
questions.explanation: Elle → -e ending → elle aime. Aimer + infinitive = like to do something. 'Elle aime chanter.'

questions.question: How do you say 'He lives in Delhi'?
questions.explanation: 'Il habite à Delhi.' Il → -e ending → il habite. 'À' before city names.

questions.question: PARLER à vs PARLER de — which is correct for 'I speak to my friend'?
questions.explanation: 'Parler à' = speak TO someone. 'Parler de' = speak ABOUT something. 'Je parle à mon ami.'

questions.question: Make a sentence: ils / habiter / à / Lyon
questions.explanation: Ils → -ent → ils habitent. 'Ils habitent à Lyon.' = They live in Lyon.

questions.question: Which sentence is WRONG?
questions.explanation: 'Ils habitez' is wrong — ils takes -ent, not -ez. Correct: 'Ils habitent en France.'

questions.question: Translate: 'Do you (tu) like Paris?'
questions.explanation: 'Tu aimes Paris?' In French, questions can be formed by rising intonation alone: 'Tu aimes Paris?' (tu + -es ending).

questions.question: Make a mini text: 'Je/habiter/Paris. J'aimer/la Tour Eiffel.'
options: J'habite à Paris. J'aime la Tour Eiffel.
Je habite Paris. J'aimes la Tour Eiffel.
J'habite Paris. J'aimez la Tour Eiffel.
J'habitons Paris. J'aiment la Tour Eiffel.
questions.explanation: J'habite à Paris (je + habite + à + city). J'aime la Tour Eiffel (je + aime). Both -ER verbs, correct endings.
